## Common Mistakes

- Titling head forward can shift weight to the balls of the feet, placing excess stress on the body, and cause rounding of the back
- Tilting head backward can shift weight to the heels of the feet, causing an improper curvature of the spine and unwanted stress on the neck and back

## Foot Position

1. Narrow stance - works quadriceps and gluteals to some extent
2. Medium stance - works quadriceps and adductors to some extent
3. Wide stance - works adductor, gluteus, and outer quadriceps
4. Keep heels on the floor
5. Point toes out slightly from neutral to 30°
6. The angle of the foot position makes no difference as long as you are comfortable with the stance

## Common Mistakes

- Not finding what stance works for you
- Turning or pointing the toes inward
